html:
Jigme Dorji Wangchuck was the third king of Bhutan, from 1952 to 1972, remembered as the father of modern Bhutan. He was born in 1928 at Thruepang Palace in Trongsa.

When he came to the throne, Bhutan had no roads, no paper money and almost no schools. He set up a National Assembly in 1953, freed the serfs, reformed land holding and made Thimphu the capital. After China's takeover of Tibet closed the old trade routes north, he turned south to India, which built the first motor roads and paid for the first five-year plans.

He brought Bhutan into the United Nations in 1971, a year before his death in Nairobi. His son Jigme Singye Wangchuck carried on his work and coined Gross National Happiness. The family's dynasty still reigns.
